journey.name: XR - Spatial Shell, Panes and Video
journey.description:
Verifies the Android XR experience on a headset or XR glasses (Android XR emulator XR_Headset, Galaxy XR, XREAL Aura): the navigation capsule inside the panel in Home Space, the leading navigation Orbiter outside the panel in Full Space, list-detail panes on the wide default panel, and the fullscreen video player driven by pinch (tap) input. The relaunch below restarts the app, so it does not cover state surviving an in-session Home Space / Full Space switch; check that by hand with the title-bar button on a device.
Run with the bench build. Launch in Home Space normally; to enter Full Space without the title-bar button (adb input taps on it do not register on the emulator), relaunch with adb shell am force-stop net.kikin.nubecita adb shell am start --xrActivityStartMode 1 -n net.kikin.nubecita/.MainActivity and confirm with: adb shell dumpsys activity activities | grep -o "xrDesktopMode=[a-z-]*" (expect full-space-managed). A plain launch returns to Home Space.
In Home Space the capsule sitting inside the panel is by design, not a regression: Orbiters only exist in Full Space. The default panel is 1024x640dp, which is the Expanded width class, so list-detail panes are expected at the default size.
Driving it from adb: `adb shell input tap` takes panel coordinates (the bounds that `uiautomator dump --windows` reports), not screenshot pixels. The Full Space Orbiter is a separate window that injected taps never reach (they land on the panel underneath), so tap the Orbiter's destinations by hand with the emulator's mouse.
Video on the emulator: the Android XR emulator cannot play video at all (checked 2026-11-24, emulator image UP1A.231005.007.A1). Its only AVC decoder is the software one, and the GPU cannot import its YV12 frames: a TextureView player (inline feed video, vertical video feed) aborts the app's RenderThread with "Invalid GrBackendTexture", and the SurfaceView fullscreen player aborts SurfaceFlinger. Before the Full Space section, set Settings > Media and animations > Autoplay videos to Never (bench keeps it in memory until the process dies), or scrolling Discover crashes the app. Run the Fullscreen video steps on hardware (Galaxy XR, XREAL Aura) only.
Video player changes must also re-run video_player_tabletop.journey.xml on a foldable and the video steps of media_viewer.journey.xml on a phone.

actions.action: Launch the app normally and verify that it opens on the Home feed in Home Space
Verify that the navigation capsule (Feed, Search, Notifications, Chats, You) is drawn inside the panel at its leading edge, vertically centered, and does not overlap the feed
Tap the Search destination in the capsule and verify that the Search screen opens, then tap Feed to return to the Home feed
Tap a post in the feed and verify that the post thread opens in a detail pane beside the feed, with the feed still visible on the leading side
Drag the feed pane up several posts and verify that it scrolls smoothly while the detail pane stays in place
Relaunch the app in Full Space
Verify that the navigation capsule now floats outside the panel, to the left of its leading edge, and that none of it covers the feed
Verify that the feed now uses the full width of the panel with no empty strip where the capsule used to be
Tap each destination in the floating capsule (Search, Notifications, Chats, You, then Feed) and verify that each opens its screen and the selected destination is highlighted
Tap a post in the feed and verify that the thread opens in a detail pane beside the feed
Tap a post author's avatar and verify that their profile opens in the detail pane, and that only one Compose button is visible across both panes
Tap the Feed destination, tap the Discover feed chip, and drag the feed until a video post is visible and starts playing
Tap the video to open the fullscreen video player and verify that the video plays and fills the panel without being cropped
Tap an empty area of the video and verify that the Close, Skip back, Pause and Skip forward controls and the seek bar appear and are fully inside the panel
Tap Pause and verify that playback stops, then tap Play and verify that it resumes from the same position
Drag the seek bar thumb forward and verify that the elapsed time jumps forward and playback continues
Tap Close and verify that the feed is visible again, with the floating navigation capsule still outside the panel
Relaunch the app normally to return to Home Space
Verify that the navigation capsule is back inside the panel at its leading edge and the app opens on the Home feed without a crash or a sign-in screen
